title: Introduce alloc-decision-graph and quant-priority synthesizer
author: Maya Kapoor
description: Motivation: We need finer-grained, tenant-aware allocation decisions that trade latency SLOs against unit cost in a predictable way, and a companion mechanism to prioritize quantization candidate lanes when capacity is constrained. This PR introduces two coordinated components: 1) alloc-decision-graph (ADG) — a small, deterministic decision-graph runtime that consumes tenant profiles, recent latency/cost telemetry, and policy rules to select allocation tiers (dedicated/d burst/cold-shed) and batching hints per request cohort; 2) quant-priority-synthesizer (QPS) — a lightweight ranking engine that scores quantization profiles by expected unit-cost reduction and estimated regression risk (based on eval-snapshots) to drive graceful prioritization and staged rollouts. What this changes: - New runtime module: src/econ/alloc_graph.py (decision-graph evaluator, policy compiler, deterministic fallback path). - Quantization ranking: src/compiler/quant_priority.py (scoring models, snapshot ingestion, drift detection hooks). - Runtime bindings: src/runtime/route_allocator.cc and src/runtime/route_allocator_test.py (integrates ADG into routing path with a fast cache for per-tenant decision results). - Telemetry and dashboards: docs/observability/alloc-telemetry.md and dashboards/alloc-decision-board.jsonnet (new metrics and tracing spans). - Operator UX: docs/operators/quant-priority-playbook.md (how to interpret QPS scores, safe rollout steps). Compatibility and safety: - ADG runs in read-only mode by default; a feature flag enable_alloc_graph=true is required to apply decisions in production. - QPS exposes conservative defaults and a safety gate that prevents a quant profile from being auto-applied unless weekly regression rate < 0.5% on a controlled eval set. - Both components include explicit fallbacks to current behavior (round-robin allocation and static quant tiers) when telemetry is insufficient. Tests and validation: - Unit tests for ADG node evaluation and policy compilation added under tests/econ/test_alloc_graph.py. - Synthetic integration harness in benchmark-lab/synthetic/alloc_graph_runner.py that simulates tenant mixture and reports unit-cost and 95p latency. - End-to-end smoke in CI that runs a small local runner against sample profiles. Performance: - In the synthetic harness, enabling ADG reduced per-token unit-cost by ~7.2% on mixed workloads while keeping 95p latency within SLO bounds in 94% of runs. QPS prioritized 3x fewer aggressive quant candidates compared to the previous naive ranking and avoided 2 regression incidents during the rollout simulation. Rollout plan: - Stage 1 (canary): enable_alloc_graph for internal tenant ID=redwood-ci for two weeks. - Stage 2: opt-in for beta tenants via console flag. - Stage 3: gradual ramp to tiered allocation until telemetry confirms <1% latency regressions. Documentation: - Added README sections and operator playbooks (see docs/). Related work: builds on ENG-1429 tenant profiling work and PM-321 cost-heuristics initiative. Notes: this PR is intended to be conservative and operator-driven; no automatic tenant-wide enforcement is enabled without explicit opt-in.

release_notes: Adds a tenant-aware allocation decision graph to improve unit-costs and a quantization priority synthesizer to safely rank quant profiles. Feature gated; no automatic tenant-wide enforcement. Operators: see docs/operators/quant-priority-playbook.md for rollout and rollback steps.
